title: Additive representations by powerful integers
summary: Pointwise bounds for powerful sums and differences, and primitive-triple bounds for diagonal, restricted mixed, and consecutive powerfulness orders, with a full leading saving on the consecutive family.
abstract:
For fixed \(k\ge2\), let \(r_k(N)\) count ordered representations of \(N\)
as a sum of two positive \(k\)-full integers. We prove
\(r_2(N)\ll_\varepsilon N^{3/10+\varepsilon}\) and
\(r_k(N)\ll_{k,\varepsilon}N^{1/(k+1)+\varepsilon}\) for \(k\ge3\).
The proof bounds the number of common neighbors in bipartite graphs formed
by omitting one coordinate of the canonical factorization.
The graph bounds also apply to coprime differences of size at least
\(X^{2/k}\) between \(k\)-full integers bounded by \(X\), for \(k\ge3\).
Applying the individual graph bounds to primitive \(k\)-full triples
\(a+b=c\le X\) gives \(O_{k,\varepsilon}(X^{2/(k+1)+\varepsilon})\) triples for
every fixed \(k\ge3\). For primitive triples of orders
\(p=r+u,\ q=r+v,\ r\) with fixed offsets, a mixed-exponent graph gives
a saving \(2/r^2+O_{u,v}(r^{-3})\) over \(1/p+1/q\) when the four
gcds of the first two exponents on the summand sides are at least four.
For \((p,q,r)=(r+2,r+1,r)\), a coefficient-uniform point-counting
estimate makes the graph bounds effective with gcd two and gives
a leading saving of \(2/r^2\) for all sufficiently large \(r\).
For even \(r\) we group two omitted coordinates into a single
square variable.
